The user requests to secure a flight reservation from SF to Rome Oct 10 2026 business class using card id card_7243 and access token abc123xyz. Also need to convert ticket cost to EUR.

We have no direct knowledge of price; we can fetch flight cost via get_flight_cost (travel_from=SanFrancisco? Actually city names enumerated include San Francisco). But get_flight_cost expects travel_from as 3-letter code of departing airport. We don't know the IATA code for San Francisco Airport - it's SFO. For Rome's main international airport, that's FCO (Rome–Fiumicino International Airport) but maybe also CAG etc. We'll assume FCO.

So step1: get_flight_cost(travel_from="SFO", travel_to="FCO", travel_date="2026-10-10", travel_class="business"). That returns cost in USD.

Then convert to EUR using compute_exchange_rate(base_currency="USD", target_currency="EUR", value=<cost>).

Finally book_flight(access_token='abc123xyz', card_id='card_7243', travel_date='2026-10-10', travel_from='SFO', travel_to='FCO', travel_class='business').

But before booking, ensure within user's budget? Not requested explicitly. Just align with financial constraints. Might check budget limit? No info about budget. So proceed.

Thus calls:

First get_flight_cost -> store result.

Second compute_exchange_rate -> store conversion.

Third book_flight.

We'll do them sequentially.
